title: Garden and Choir Again
premise: Astrid Halloran, last apprentice of the Lanternwright Guild, survives by selling harmless charms in Corvane, a city where magic is a hanging offense. When a dying courier leaves her a map to the Hollow Choir—the vanished singers who once maintained the covenant binding the human realm to the wild Faeheart—she learns the covenant's silence is why the seasons are failing and why the guild died. Hunted by the Inquisitor Veyra and betrayed by the mentor who helped outlaw magic to save his own skin, Astrid must gather the scattered remnant of the Choir and carry their song back to the Faeheart. She succeeds only by sacrificing her own memories of the people she loves, reforging the covenant at the cost of everything that made her want to save it—until the final chapter asks whether what was given up can ever be sung home again.
about_author: Marguerite Brightwater is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk songs in coastal fishing towns before turning to fiction. Her work blends ballad structure with quiet, stubborn heroines, and 'Garden and Choir Again' is her second novel.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Winter
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. On the frozen streets of Corvane she sells luck-knots and fever-charms to desperate customers while hiding her guild mark beneath her sleeve. A raid on the market nearly catches her; an old woman shields her at terrible cost. The beat establishes fear as habit and loneliness as armor.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Door
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A bloodied stranger collapses in her cellar workshop, raving about the Hollow Choir. He presses a wax-sealed map into her hands and dies whispering her guild name—a name no one should know. The emotional beat: terror mixed with the first flicker of purpose in three years.

chapters.title: What the Map Remembers
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Studying the map, Astrid finds it drawn in living ink that shifts to show the failing seasons. It marks seven resting places of the Choir's scattered members. She burns her remaining charms and packs. Beat: grief for the safe life she is choosing to abandon.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Kindness
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. The Inquisitor Veyra interrogates the market witnesses, courteous and patient, and identifies Astrid from a child's description. We learn she keeps a private collection of confiscated charms she cannot bring herself to destroy. Beat: the antagonist revealed as sincere, not cruel.

chapters.title: Road Through Ashfield
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Traveling north, Astrid passes villages where crops grow black and children have stopped dreaming. She uses forbidden magic openly for the first time to heal a farmer's blight—and is seen doing it. Beat: exhilaration curdling into exposure.

chapters.title: The First Voice
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At a drowned chapel she finds Sera Ilvane, a Choir singer grown mute from despair, tending a garden that still blooms impossibly. Astrid's guild training lets her hear the garden's song when Sera cannot speak it. Beat: hope, fragile and green.

chapters.title: Old Debts
chapters.summary: Master Corren's POV. Flashback-tinged chapter: Corren, Astrid's former mentor, now a respected magistrate, receives word of the map and realizes his old crime—helping outlaw magic—is unraveling. He sends riders after her. Beat: guilt wearing the mask of duty.

chapters.title: Hunted Through the Fen
chapters.summary: Astrid and Sera's POV, alternating. Pursued by Veyra's riders through the marshes, they shelter with fen-witches who remember the covenant and hate humans for breaking it. Sera regains a single word of her voice: 'run.' Beat: loyalty tested by survival.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. They find Tam Breck, a Choir drummer turned drunkard in a mining town, who refuses to sing again because his music once killed a man during the purges. Astrid offers him neither forgiveness nor judgment—only the truth of the dying world. Beat: anger giving way to reluctant commitment.

chapters.title: Veyra Closes In
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. Veyra captures one of the fen-witches and learns the covenant's true stakes: without it, the Faeheart will not merely fade but bleed its wildness into the human realm. She begins to doubt which side justice lies on. Beat: conviction cracking.

chapters.title: The Traitor's House
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The map leads Astrid to Corren's own estate—he is the third voice, a former Choir cantor. Their confrontation is the book's moral center: he outlawed magic believing the covenant was already dead and order was mercy. Beat: betrayal and unbearable understanding.

chapters.title: Chains and Choices
chapters.summary: Corren's POV. Corren turns Astrid over to Veyra to protect his position, then spends a sleepless night with his confiscated guild relics. He releases her secretly, giving her his cantor's bell, and stays behind to face arrest. Beat: redemption purchased too late to be clean.

chapters.title: Prison of Quiet
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Recaptured anyway, Astrid waits in Veyra's cells, where wards strip her of magic. Veyra visits not to torture but to talk, showing Astrid her charm collection and asking what magic has ever actually given the poor. Beat: doubt planted deep.

chapters.title: The Escape That Costs
chapters.summary: Tam and Sera's POV. The two singers break Astrid out, but Sera is gravely wounded holding the ward-line open. Fleeing east with Sera fading, Astrid realizes the Choir needs more than voices—it needs a reason to sing. Beat: sacrifice sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: The Garden Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Guided by the map's final page, they reach the entrance to the Faeheart: a garden growing inside a hollow mountain, tended by creatures half-forgotten. Here Astrid learns the covenant's price—any mortal who reforges it must give the Faeheart their dearest memories as kindling. Beat: dread and awe entwined.

chapters.title: What Astrid Would Lose
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Alone, Astrid inventorying her memories realizes her dearest are of her dead mother and of Corren teaching her first song. She tries to choose shallower memories and fails—the Faeheart accepts nothing false. Beat: the theme made flesh: loyalty vs. truth, love vs. duty.

chapters.title: Veyra's Turn
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. Having verified the failing seasons herself, Veyra arrives at the mountain—not to arrest Astrid but to ask what she can do. Astrid, stunned, gives her the choice freely. Veyra offers her soldiers' voices to swell the Choir. Beat: enemy becoming ally, earned not given.

chapters.title: The Hollow Choir Assembles
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. In the garden, the ragged Choir gathers: Sera carried on a bier, Tam with his drum, Corren escaped from custody and limping in, Veyra's soldiers uncertain. They rehearse the covenant-song and fail—the kindling is insufficient. Beat: unity achieved, victory withheld.

chapters.title: The Song and the Price
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Climax. Astrid steps into the Faeheart's heart and sings, surrendering her mother's face, Corren's lessons, her own name's history. The covenant blazes back to life; seasons turn audibly; the wild and human realms lock hands again. Beat: triumph inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Corvane
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Magic is decriminalized in the covenant's wake; Corren publicly confesses and accepts exile; Veyra resigns rather than enforce dead laws. Astrid returns to the city and does not recognize the market where she once sold charms. Beat: justice achieved, home estranged.

chapters.title: Garden Without a Gardener
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Sera, voice restored, tends the drowned chapel garden and grieves for Astrid's emptiness. Tam begins teaching new singers. The guild mark on Astrid's arm glows faintly whenever someone nearby remembers her kindly. Beat: tenderness amid irreversibility.

chapters.title: Choir Again
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Final chapter. A memory arrives unbidden—a lullaby she doesn't recall learning—and Astrid realizes the Faeheart is slowly returning what was given, one song at a time, across years. She opens a small shop selling charms again, legally, and hums along. Beat: quiet, hard-won hope.
